decision: Sample requests filed 1 Jan 2025 to 31 Aug 2026
why: Every promise date has passed; matches the brief
alternative_rejected: Through 12 Oct 2026 (recent requests could still gain attachments)

decision: 20 largest hand-off pairs from build/R1/handoff_composition.csv x40, 10 largest done codes x30, 10 largest open-past-promise codes x30, split evenly across ward groups 1-5, 6-9, 10-14
why: As briefed; ward split stops one area's practice dominating a stratum
alternative_rejected: Simple random sample (would be mostly refuse and towing)

decision: Add 'Inspect City Tree | removal work order created' as a named stratum H_tree (40)
why: It is the positive control the thesis rests on and is not among the 20 largest hand-off pairs (390 requests in window)
alternative_rejected: Rely on the orchestrator's two tree pages

decision: Order within each cell by md5('E1-status-page-2026-10-14' || request_id)
why: Reproducible without depending on DuckDB thread scheduling

decision: Measure = hidden <span id=totalItem> counter > 0; call it 'any attached item'
why: The counter covers inspections and work orders; the panel's rows come from a disallowed endpoint robots.txt disallows and we never call
alternative_rejected: Calling dsp-related-items.cfc to separate work orders from inspections

decision: Stopped fetching after 2 pages and asked the orchestrator
why: robots.txt, under User-agent: *, says '#added 05/18/11 - Ben D - Do not crawl service request, board bills, etc.' then 'Disallow: check-service-request.cfm'. The rule lacks a leading slash, so RFC 9309 parsers (Python robotparser: can_fetch=True) match nothing, but the owner's intent is explicit
alternative_rejected: Proceed on the technical reading without a ruling

decision: Stage a 152-id subset of the drawn sample (8 strata, 18-20 each, ward-balanced) for a 3-minute run if Jack approves
why: Smallest set that separates 0% from ~50% per service while minimising load on a page robots.txt asks bots to avoid
alternative_rejected: Full 1,440 (25 min of automated reads against stated intent)

decision: Ran the full 1,440 pages and the related-items endpoint after Jack's ruling (relayed about 3:23 p.m., 14 Oct 2026)
why: Jack reports city staff authorised crawling the city's sites for this project at office hours that day; robots.txt concern stated in the report

decision: One file-locked clock shared by the page fetcher and the items reader: at most one request per 1.05 s to www.stlouis-mo.gov
why: Two processes against one host must not double the rate
alternative_rejected: Run items only after all pages (slower; same rate)

decision: Keep only allowlisted item fields on disk; log SHA-256 and size of each raw response instead of saving it
why: The allowlist rule says filter before saving; a raw response could carry comments or names
alternative_rejected: Save raw responses in the ignored folder

decision: Keep an inspection's Result/Resolution only when it is a short upper-case code (e.g. APPROVED)
why: It is a status-like code that says whether removal was approved; free text is dropped
alternative_rejected: Drop it entirely (loses whether the inspection approved work)

decision: Grade a linked request by the first finish among work orders created on or after its filing date; Cityworks ActualFinishDate where joined, else the page's 'Completed On or Before' date; 'no finish' only where the promise passed by 13 Sep 2026
why: Mirrors R1's first-record-of-work rule and its 30-day never cutoff; excludes older work orders already open at the address
alternative_rejected: Last finish across all attached orders (would grade stump removal, not the requested job)

decision: One structure-test call to the items endpoint for a tree request at about 3:24 p.m.; response not saved; the request was read again by the run
why: Needed the response format to write the allowlist parser

decision: Keep the 12-page probe (05_probe.py) as a separate, labelled appendix; the 10 orchestrator pages are not in the sample
why: They were hand-picked; mixing them into the sample would bias shares
